articles.title: NVIDIA Releases Personal AI Router (PAIR): An Open Source Virtual Inference Router that Distributes Local AI Requests Across RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac Nodes
articles.summary: NVIDIA released Personal AI Router (PAIR), an open source virtual inference router that distributes local AI requests across machines on a home network, including RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac nodes. PAIR can proxy existing Ollama and LM Studio endpoints without requiring changes to agent harnesses, and NVIDIA showed an unofficial five-subagent demo improving average runtime from 18 minutes on one RTX Spark laptop to 8 minutes 48 seconds on a three-device cluster. The tool has limitations, including a single scheduling policy and lack of visibility into VRAM and model warmness.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a concrete example of AI infrastructure moving beyond centralized cloud data centers toward distributed local inference using existing consumer and workstation hardware. For advisors, the read-through is that NVIDIA is continuing to expand its AI ecosystem around orchestration, edge compute, and agent workflows, though PAIR appears early and developer-oriented rather than a near-term commercial product.

articles.title: Adaption Labs Introduces ‘Invent a Dataset’: Training Data Generated From a Task Description, Not a Seed Corpus
articles.summary: Adaption Labs released Invent a Dataset, an API that generates structured, training-ready datasets from a description of the behavior a user wants a model to learn. The tool requires no seed corpus, schema design, or labeling guide, and its output can be downloaded in common formats or passed directly into AutoScientist for model training.
